name: Number Slider
description: An interactive slider that outputs a number within a set range and step. Wire it into dimensions, counts or rotation angles so you can drag through design variations and watch the model respond live.

name: Integer Slider
description: A slider constrained to whole numbers, ideal for counts — panels in a facade, treads in a stair, items in a range. Use it instead of Number Slider wherever fractional values would break the logic downstream.

name: Number
description: A simple box holding a fixed numeric value. Use it for constants you want visible and labelled on the canvas rather than buried inside a code block.

name: Boolean
description: A true/false toggle used to switch logic branches, flip conditions or gate parts of a graph. Pair it with If to give a script simple on/off behaviour a non-programmer can operate.

name: String
description: A text input box outputting whatever is typed into it. The usual source for parameter names, prefixes and search terms that the rest of the graph consumes.

name: Code Block
description: A freeform node where DesignScript is typed directly — numbers, strings, ranges like 0..10..2, functions and multi-line expressions. Experienced users compress whole clusters of nodes into one tidy code block; double-click empty canvas to create one.

name: File Path
description: Opens a file browser and outputs the chosen file's path as a string. The standard front door for graphs that read Excel, images or text files.

name: Directory Path
description: Outputs the path of a chosen folder, for graphs that batch through many files or need somewhere to write exports. Combine with file-listing logic to process a whole directory of drawings or spreadsheets.

name: File.FromPath
description: Converts a path string into a file object that reading nodes can consume. A small but necessary adaptor between File Path and nodes like File.ReadText.

name: Number Range
description: Generates a list of numbers from a start to an end value at a given step — the graph equivalent of 0..100..5. The seed of most repetitive geometry: point grids, panel setout, level elevations.

name: Number Sequence
description: Generates a list by count rather than end value — start, amount and step. Use it when you know how many items you need, such as one value per panel or per level.

name: Object.IsNull
description: Returns true for null items in a list, which is the first step in cleaning data that came back patchy from Revit or Excel. Feed the result into List.FilterByBoolMask to strip the nulls out.

name: Watch
description: Displays the data flowing through a wire — values, list structure, nesting depth. The single most important debugging habit in Dynamo: watch early, watch often, and list-structure surprises get caught before they multiply.

name: Watch 3D
description: A miniature 3D viewport showing only the geometry wired into it, independent of the main background preview. Useful for isolating one branch of geometry in a busy graph.

name: Watch Image
description: Previews an image object on the canvas, for graphs that read bitmaps — heightmap-driven facades, image-sampled colour studies. Confirms the right picture is loaded before pixel values drive anything.

name: Color.ByARGB
description: Builds a colour from alpha, red, green and blue values. Feed it into display or override nodes to colour-code geometry by analysis results — area, deviation, parameter values.

name: Display.ByGeometryColor
description: Draws geometry in the preview tinted with a supplied colour, without touching Revit. The standard way to build in-canvas heat maps — remap a value to a colour range and see the gradient across your geometry.

name: Python Script
description: Embeds a Python node with access to the full Revit API, for logic that stock nodes cannot express — transactions, element filters, edge cases. The escape hatch when visual programming runs out of road; keep inputs and outputs clearly named.

name: Note
description: Places a free text note on the canvas explaining what a section of the graph does. Graphs are read far more often than written — a few notes turn a private puzzle into a tool colleagues can trust.

name: Group
description: Wraps selected nodes in a coloured, titled container — inputs, processing, outputs — so the graph reads as a storyboard. Consistent grouping and colour conventions are the mark of a shareable script.

name: Freeze
description: Right-click option that suspends a node and everything downstream of it without deleting anything. Freeze the expensive Revit-writing end of a graph while you iterate safely on the logic upstream.

name: Run (Automatic/Manual)
description: Switches the graph between re-executing on every change and running only when you press Run. Use Manual whenever the graph writes to Revit or does heavy geometry — Automatic is for lightweight exploratory work.

name: Data.OpenXMLImportExcel
description: Reads a worksheet from an Excel file into nested lists, one list per row, without needing Excel installed. The start of every spreadsheet-to-Revit workflow: room data sheets, door schedules, setting-out tables.

name: Data.OpenXMLExportExcel
description: Writes nested lists out to an Excel worksheet, starting at a given row and column. Pair with parameter-reading nodes to push live model data — areas, counts, door ironmongery — into spreadsheets others can work with.

name: Data.ParseJSON
description: Converts a JSON string into Dynamo dictionaries and lists. Useful for reading configuration files or data handed over from web services and other tools.

name: File.ReadText
description: Reads a text file into a single string, ready for splitting into lines and fields. The simple route for CSVs and logs when full Excel handling is overkill.

name: Passthrough
description: Passes its first input straight through, but only after its second input has arrived — a way to force execution order. Essential when one Revit operation must finish before another starts, which Dynamo's dataflow cannot otherwise guarantee.

name: FamilyInstance.Room
description: Returns the room each family instance sits in, closing a gap in the native node set. The key to workflows like writing room names onto furniture and equipment parameters for schedules.

name: UI.MultipleInputForm ++
description: Builds a pop-up dialog with text boxes, dropdowns and selectors so end users can run a graph without opening Dynamo. The de facto standard for turning scripts into office tools, especially via Dynamo Player.

name: List.Create
description: Bundles separate inputs into a single list, with a + button to add more ports. Use it to gather results from parallel branches before a node that expects one collection.

name: List.Map
description: Applies a function to every item in a list, returning the transformed list. Largely superseded by lacing and list levels for simple cases, but still the clearest way to run a custom function across a collection.

name: List.Combine
description: Applies a function pairwise across two or more lists — first with firsts, second with seconds. Reach for it when a straightforward wire-up mangles the pairing between corresponding items.

name: List.FilterByBoolMask
description: Splits a list into 'in' and 'out' streams according to a parallel list of true/false values. The workhorse of every selection workflow: build a test, mask the list, keep what passes.

name: List.Sort
description: Orders a list of comparable values — numbers or strings — ascending. Combine with List.Reverse for descending order.

name: List.SortByKey
description: Sorts one list using a parallel list of keys — order rooms by area, sheets by number, points by elevation. The keys travel with the items, so both come back in matching order.

name: List.Flatten
description: Collapses nested lists into a single flat list, optionally by a set number of levels. Use it deliberately — flattening everything is the quick fix that often destroys the structure a later node needed.

name: List.Chop
description: Cuts a flat list into sublists of given lengths — the inverse of flattening. Classic for rebuilding rows from a stream of values, such as turning a point list back into a grid.

name: List.Transpose
description: Swaps rows and columns in a nested list, so a list of rows becomes a list of columns. Indispensable around Excel import and export, where orientation rarely arrives the way you want it.

name: List.GetItemAtIndex
description: Pulls the item at a given position from a list, counting from zero. With a list of indices it extracts several at once — the basic tool for picking a column out of imported spreadsheet rows.

name: List.Count
description: Returns how many items a list contains. A quiet debugging hero: matching counts at both ends of an operation is the quickest sanity check that nothing got dropped.

name: List.Reverse
description: Flips the order of a list end to end. Useful after sorting, or for correcting curve and boundary directions expressed as point lists.

name: List.FirstItem
description: Returns the first item of a list. Commonly used to strip a header row's partner, grab a single test element or peel one sample from a big set while developing.

name: List.LastItem
description: Returns the final item of a list, whatever its length. Handy for end points of point sequences and the newest item of sorted data.

name: List.Contains
description: Tests whether a list includes a given item, returning true or false. Use it to check membership against an approved list — type names, level names — before acting.

name: List.IndexOf
description: Returns the position of an item within a list, or -1 if absent. Pair with List.GetItemAtIndex to look values up across parallel lists, dictionary-style.

name: List.Join
description: Concatenates several lists into one continuous list, preserving order. Unlike List.Create, which nests its inputs, Join splices them end to end.

name: List.UniqueItems
description: Removes duplicates, keeping the first occurrence of each value. The standard first move for building a clean set of type names, materials or levels actually used in a model.

name: List.GroupByKey
description: Buckets items into sublists according to matching keys — rooms grouped by department, walls by type name. Returns both the groups and their unique keys, ready for per-group processing or reporting.

name: List.TakeItems
description: Keeps the first n items of a list (or the last n with a negative count). Useful for sampling a subset while testing, or trimming a list to a known length.

name: List.DropItems
description: Discards the first n items of a list (or the last n with a negative count). The classic way to skip a header row from imported spreadsheet data.

name: List.AddItemToEnd
description: Appends a single item to the end of a list. Small but constant duty in assembling rows for export or closing loops of points.

name: List.IsEmpty
description: Returns true when a list has no items. Wire it into conditional logic so a graph fails gracefully when a selection or filter comes back with nothing.

name: List.Cycle
description: Repeats a list a given number of times end to end. Useful for tiling patterns — alternate panel types, repeated colour sequences — across a longer set of targets.

name: If
description: Chooses between two inputs according to a boolean test — true takes the first, false the second. The basic branching node; combine with comparison nodes to make graphs respond to conditions.

name: And
description: Returns true only when all its boolean inputs are true. Use it to combine tests — right category and right level — before filtering.

name: Or
description: Returns true when any of its boolean inputs is true. The partner to And for building compound conditions.

name: Not
description: Inverts a boolean — true becomes false and vice versa. Often the quickest way to flip a filter, keeping what a test rejected.
Tests whether two values are equal, returning true or false, and laces across lists to test many at once. The seed of most filtering: compare parameter values to a target and mask the results.

name: Math.RemapRange
description: Rescales a list of numbers from their current spread to a new minimum and maximum. The engine behind data-driven design — remap distances to panel openings, areas to colours, anything to anything.

name: Math.Round
description: Rounds a number to the nearest whole value or given number of decimals. Tidy values before writing them into parameters or spreadsheets that humans will read.

name: Math.Floor
description: Rounds a number down to the nearest integer. Useful for working out how many whole units — panels, treads, tiles — fit within a dimension.

name: Math.Ceiling
description: Rounds a number up to the nearest integer. The counterpart to Math.Floor when you need to be sure of covering a dimension rather than fitting inside it.

name: Math.Abs
description: Returns the absolute value of a number, stripping the sign. Common in tolerance checks where only the size of a difference matters, not its direction.

name: Math.Sin
description: Returns the sine of an angle given in degrees. Feed it a number range to generate wave forms for undulating facades, ceilings and screens.

name: Math.Cos
description: Returns the cosine of an angle given in degrees. With Math.Sin it converts angles into x and y components for radial arrays and circular setout.

name: Math.PI
description: Outputs the constant pi. Used in circumference, arc-length and radian conversions inside geometric setout.

name: String.Concat
description: Joins several strings into one, in port order. The standard way to build parameter values like room codes from prefix, number and suffix parts.

name: String.Split
description: Cuts a string into a list wherever a separator occurs — commas for CSV rows, hyphens for door numbers. The first move in parsing any structured text.

name: String.Join
description: Combines a list of strings into one, inserting a separator between each. The inverse of String.Split, used to reassemble codes and to build readable report lines.

name: String.Contains
description: Tests whether a string includes a given fragment, returning true or false. Combined with a filter it finds every type name containing a keyword — all walls with 'EX', all views with 'WIP'.

name: String.Replace
description: Swaps every occurrence of a fragment within a string for new text. The engine of batch renaming workflows — views, sheets, family types — when paired with name-setting nodes.

name: String.ToNumber
description: Parses a string into a numeric value. Necessary after Excel import or text parameters, where numbers often arrive disguised as text and refuse to calculate.

name: String from Object
description: Converts any value — number, element, boolean — into its text representation. Use it before concatenation or export, and for readable debugging output.

name: String.ToUpper
description: Converts a string to upper case. Useful for enforcing drawing-standard capitalisation on names and title text, or normalising values before comparison.

name: Point.ByCoordinates
description: Creates a point from x, y and z values, and with list inputs and lacing settings, whole grids of points at once. The atom of computational geometry — most parametric setout begins here.

name: Point.Origin
description: Outputs the point at 0,0,0. A convenient anchor for base planes, coordinate systems and geometry that will be moved into place later.

name: Vector.ByCoordinates
description: Creates a direction vector from x, y and z components. Vectors carry direction and magnitude for translations, extrusions and normals — they position nothing by themselves.

name: Vector.XAxis
description: Outputs the unit vector along the world x axis. A ready-made direction for offsets, arrays and mirror axes without building a vector by hand.

name: Vector.ZAxis
description: Outputs the unit vector pointing straight up the world z axis. The default direction for vertical extrusions, level offsets and rotation axes in plan.

name: Plane.ByOriginNormal
description: Creates a plane from a point on it and a vector perpendicular to it. Planes serve as mirrors, section cutters and hosts for sketch-like operations throughout the geometry library.

name: Plane.XY
description: Outputs the world ground plane at the origin. The usual base for flat setout and a quick mirror or section plane at level zero.

name: CoordinateSystem.ByOrigin
description: Creates a coordinate system located at a given point, axes aligned to the world. Transform nodes can then move, rotate and scale geometry relative to it rather than the world origin.

name: Line.ByStartPointEndPoint
description: Creates a straight line between two points, and with paired lists, whole families of lines at once. The basic stroke for setout, structure lines and edges that later become walls or beams.

name: Line.ByStartPointDirectionLength
description: Creates a line from a start point, a direction vector and a length. Preferable to two-point construction when the geometry is naturally described as origin plus direction, such as grid rays.

name: Arc.ByThreePoints
description: Fits a circular arc through three points — start, a point on the curve and end. Handy for curved walls and paths defined by survey or setting-out points rather than centre and radius.

name: Circle.ByCenterPointRadius
description: Creates a circle from a centre point and radius, optionally on a given normal. A frequent base curve for radial setout, columns of points and extruded cylinders.

name: Rectangle.ByWidthLength
description: Creates a closed rectangle of given width and length, centred on a plane or coordinate system. A quick closed profile for floor outlines, panel boundaries and extrusion bases.

name: Polygon.ByPoints
description: Connects a list of points into a closed polygon, joining the last point back to the first. Use it for boundary outlines destined to become floors, regions or extrusion profiles.

name: PolyCurve.ByPoints
description: Chains a list of points into a connected polycurve, open or closed. The workhorse for paths and boundaries built from computed point lists, feeding walls, railings and sweeps.

name: NurbsCurve.ByPoints
description: Fits a smooth freeform curve through a list of points. The route to flowing geometry — sinuous walls, sculpted rails — from a handful of control locations.

name: Curve.PointAtParameter
description: Returns the point at a normalised position along a curve, 0 at the start and 1 at the end. Feed it a range of parameters to sprinkle points along any curve for panels, mullions or planting.

name: Curve.PointsAtEqualSegmentLength
description: Divides a curve into segments of equal length and returns the division points. The honest way to space elements evenly along a curve, since equal parameter steps are not equal distances on most curves.

name: Curve.Length
description: Returns the length of a curve in model units. Sums neatly across lists for quick take-offs of skirting runs, kerb lines or duct routes.

name: Curve.Offset
description: Creates a parallel copy of a curve at a set distance, sign controlling the side. Used for wall centrelines to faces, path edges and nested boundary patterns.

name: Curve.Extrude
description: Sweeps a curve along a direction vector to create a surface. The quick way to raise a fence of surfaces from plan curves — walls-to-be, screens, ribbons.

name: Curve.ExtrudeAsSolid
description: Extrudes a closed curve into a solid of given distance. The one-step massing tool: draw a footprint, extrude it, and interrogate volume or intersections immediately.

name: Surface.ByPatch
description: Fills a closed curve with a flat surface, like stretching a skin across a boundary. The standard step between a closed outline and area measurement or solid modelling.

name: Surface.ByLoft
description: Skins a smooth surface through an ordered list of cross-section curves. The primary tool for doubly-curved facades, canopies and terrain-like surfaces from profile families.

name: Surface.PointAtParameter
description: Returns the point at a u,v position on a surface, 0 to 1 in each direction. Cross two ranges and you have a point grid draped over any surface — the seed of panelling workflows.

name: Surface.NormalAtParameter
description: Returns the vector perpendicular to a surface at a u,v position. Essential for orienting panels and components so they sit flush on curved surfaces rather than all facing one way.

name: Surface.Thicken
description: Gives a surface physical depth, producing a solid, optionally thickened both sides. The usual last step before turning abstract skins into wall-like or slab-like solids for import or clash checks.

name: Surface.Area
description: Returns the area of a surface in model units. Combined with patching room or facade boundaries, it powers quick comparative area studies outside the Revit schedule system.

name: Cuboid.ByLengths
description: Creates a box solid of given width, length and height about an origin. The quickest test solid for massing studies, clash proxies and bounding volumes.

name: Sphere.ByCenterPointRadius
description: Creates a sphere solid from a centre and radius. Often used as a visual marker at key points or as a soft proxy for clearance zones around equipment.

name: Solid.Union
description: Fuses two or more solids into one. Use it to consolidate massing pieces before measuring volume or exporting a single clean object.

name: Solid.Difference
description: Subtracts one solid from another, carving openings, courtyards and cuts. With massing solids it answers questions like how much volume remains after removing circulation.

name: Geometry.Translate
description: Moves geometry by a vector or by x, y, z distances, returning a moved copy. With lists and lacing it becomes an array engine — one profile stepped along a range makes a whole set.

name: Geometry.Rotate
description: Rotates geometry about an origin and axis by an angle in degrees. Feed it a list of angles for radial arrays and twisting stacked-floor studies.

name: Geometry.Scale
description: Scales geometry uniformly or per axis about a base point. Useful for unit fixes on imported geometry and for graded families of shapes in pattern studies.

name: Geometry.Mirror
description: Reflects geometry about a plane, returning the mirrored copy. Use world planes for quick handing or a constructed plane for arbitrary mirror lines.

name: Geometry.Intersect
description: Returns the shared geometry where two inputs overlap — a plane through a solid yields section curves, two solids yield their common volume. A core analytical tool for slicing and overlap studies.

name: Geometry.Split
description: Cuts geometry into pieces using another piece of geometry as the knife — a plane through a solid, a curve across a surface. Returns all fragments for you to keep or discard.

name: Geometry.Trim
description: Splits geometry with a cutting tool and discards the side nearest a picked point, keeping the rest. The tidy alternative to Split when you already know which portion should survive.

name: Geometry.DistanceTo
description: Measures the shortest distance between two pieces of geometry. Across lists it builds proximity fields — distance from each panel to an attractor point — that drive data-responsive designs.

name: Geometry.DoesIntersect
description: Returns true if two pieces of geometry touch or overlap. A lightweight clash and containment test — which desks fall inside a zone, which pipes cross a wall.

name: Geometry.BoundingBox
description: Returns the axis-aligned box that just encloses geometry. Useful for overall sizes, spatial sorting and generating simplified proxies for heavy elements.

name: Select Model Element
description: Lets you click one element in the Revit view and brings it into the graph. The simplest bridge from model to script — ideal while developing, before switching to category-wide selection.

name: Select Model Elements
description: Lets you window-select or pick multiple Revit elements into the graph as a list. Use it for ad hoc sets; prefer rule-based collection when the workflow must be repeatable on other models.

name: Select Face
description: Picks a single face of a Revit element and imports it as a Dynamo surface. The gateway to panelling or measuring real model geometry — a facade face, a roof plane, a wall surface.

name: Categories
description: A dropdown of every Revit category — Walls, Doors, Rooms — outputting the chosen one. Almost always the first node of a collection chain feeding All Elements of Category.

name: All Elements of Category
description: Collects every element of a chosen category in the model into one list. The standard opening move of audit and batch-edit workflows — all rooms, all doors, all views, in one wire.

name: Element Types
description: A dropdown of Revit API class types — FamilyType, Level, View — for type-based collection. Pairs with All Elements of Type to gather things that category selection reaches awkwardly.

name: All Elements of Type
description: Collects every element of a chosen API class into a list — all levels, all view templates, all family types. The partner to Element Types for model-management graphs.

name: Family Types
description: A dropdown listing every loaded family type in the project, outputting the chosen one. Feeds placement nodes like FamilyInstance.ByPoint with the type to place.

name: Levels
description: A dropdown of the project's levels, outputting the chosen level element. Placement and creation nodes — floors, walls, family instances — take it as their host input.

name: Element.GetParameterValueByName
description: Reads a named parameter's value from elements — Area from rooms, Mark from doors, Comments from anything. Half of the fundamental read-modify-write pattern behind almost every data workflow in Dynamo.

name: Element.SetParameterByName
description: Writes a value into a named parameter on elements, in bulk. The other half of read-modify-write — renumbering doors, stamping room data, syncing spreadsheet values into the model. Run in Manual mode and check units and storage types first.

name: Element.Parameters
description: Lists every parameter an element carries, with names and values. The discovery tool for finding exactly what a parameter is called before wiring up get or set nodes.

name: Element.Name
description: Returns the name of an element or type — level names, view names, family type names. A staple for filtering by naming convention and for building reports.

name: Element.Id
description: Returns the element's unique Revit ID. Useful in reports and logs so a human can trace a flagged item back in Revit with Select by ID.

name: Element.Geometry
description: Extracts an element's geometry as native Dynamo solids and surfaces, ready for measurement, intersection or export. Heavy on big selections — pull geometry from filtered lists, not entire categories.

name: Element.GetLocation
description: Returns the placement geometry of elements — a point for most families, a curve for walls and beams. The starting point for spatial sorting, setting-out exports and moving things by rule.

name: Element.OverrideColorInView
description: Overrides the colour of elements in the active Revit view, driven from the graph. The classic model-audit trick: colour every element by parameter value and see problems instantly on screen.

name: FamilyInstance.ByPoint
description: Places a family instance of a given type at each input point — hundreds of columns, planting or fixtures in one run. Feed it computed point sets to turn setout logic directly into placed Revit content.

name: Wall.ByCurveAndHeight
description: Creates Revit walls along input curves at a given height, level and wall type. The bridge from generative plan layouts — traced, imported or computed — to real, schedulable walls.

name: Floor.ByOutlineTypeAndLevel
description: Creates a Revit floor from a closed outline of curves, a floor type and a level. Useful for regenerating slabs from computed footprints or batch-building floors across many levels.

name: Level.ByElevation
description: Creates Revit levels at given elevations. Wire in a range and generate a tower's worth of consistently spaced, consistently named levels in seconds.

name: Grid.ByLine
description: Creates Revit grids from input lines. Combined with ranges and translated lines, it sets out an entire numbered grid system from a few parameters — spacing, count, extent.

name: Sheet.ByNameNumberTitleBlockAndViews
description: Creates sheets from lists of names and numbers, a title block type and views to place. The heart of sheet automation — a spreadsheet of the drawing list becomes the actual drawing set.

name: FloorPlanView.ByLevel
description: Creates a floor plan view for each input level. With Level.ByElevation and sheet nodes it forms the project set-up chain: levels, then plans, then sheets, all generated to standard.

name: ImportInstance.ByGeometry
description: Pushes Dynamo geometry into Revit as an import instance — a quick way to get computed solids and surfaces visible in the project. Good for massing and placeholders; convert to families when elements need data and categories.
